# DialSQL: Dialogue Based Structured Query Generation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#dialsql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/P18-1124.pdf) · ACL 2018 proceedings, pages 1339-1349

**Reading coverage:** All 11 PDF pages: Sections 1-6, equations, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-4 and references. Human-evaluation table and preference plot visually checked.

## Research question

Repair a base parser's SQL through short validation questions understandable without SQL expertise.

## Method

A hierarchical RNN predicts error category, token span and replacement choices. Training dialogues reverse synthetic query mutations; the simulator consults reference SQL. The interface uses table headers rather than cell contents.

## Evaluation

WikiSQL query-match accuracy, dialogue length and question token count; a separate 100-question development sample is evaluated with three user judgments per dialogue.

## What the results support

Five-choice interaction raises SQLNet test query-match accuracy from 61.3% to 69.0%. On the smaller human-study sample, baseline, simulated-user and real-user scores are 58%, 75% and 65%, respectively.

## Limits and qualifications

Single-table WikiSQL and template-based interaction limit transfer. Ideal reference-aware feedback overestimates real-user performance; users can reject all offered choices, and headers may not resolve value meanings.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An early interactive repair baseline with actual human evidence, but not an ambiguity taxonomy or refusal benchmark.
